title: Level 5 (World Class) - C-3
notes:
West leads the ♦Q against 6NT. Assuming the hearts produce 5 tricks, South has 11 top tricks. If East has the ♠K then South can win a twelfth trick by leading toward his ♠Q. Alternatively, a 3-2 diamond break could provide South with the extra trick that he needs.

Furthermore, South may be able to succeed with a squeeze if either defender (presumably West) was dealt 4 diamonds and the ♠K. South may be tempted to allow West's diamond opening lead to win in an effort to rectify the count for a possible squeeze. West can shift to a spade, however, and South won't know if he should win dummy's ♠A or not.

If the ♠A is played, it will be impossible to squeeze West (as he is sitting over both South's spades and diamonds). If instead South plays a low spade from dummy, he will go down when East was dealt the ♠K and diamonds were 3-2.

South must resist the temptation to duck the first trick. He should win West's diamond opening lead, unblock the hearts, and test the diamonds by cashing South's remaining honor. If both defenders follow, South can give up a diamond trick to establish his twelfth trick in that suit. If, instead, East discards on the second round of diamonds, South can still succeed with a 2-loser squeeze when West has the ♠K along with his known diamond length.

South can cross to the dummy in clubs and run dummy's hearts followed by South's clubs. When South leads his last club winner West is squeezed in spades and diamonds. West cannot afford to bare his ♠K and a diamond discard allows South to succeed by pitching either a small spade or a diamond from dummy. In either case South leads a diamond next and either sets up a diamond trick or endplays West (depending on what is discarded from dummy).

This is, in fact, a deceptively simple deal. After South cashes the second round of diamonds and discovers West was dealt 4 cards in that suit, East becomes an odds on favorite to hold the ♠K. South should play a spade to dummy's ♠A and lead a low spade toward the ♠Q, hoping East was dealt the ♠K.
